What I notice about children is I feel like they're having the hardest time when they're kind of quiet and they kind of keep to themselves. There was a time where our classroom, when I first became the lead teacher at Laugh and Learn, and our class just got like a flood of kids. So the newer kids kind of like tested the limits and then wouldn't listen. And then the kids that had been there for a long time were kind of like they knew the routine. For a moment, it did get out of control in the room, but I kind of just took like a deep breath. And like I kind of like just told myself like, you have it, you're okay. Like it's going to be just fine. Like they trust you, like you're in control. You know, they're whatever you say. They're going to do, they're going to listen. And it kind of brings me down when I kind of like, instead of spiraling, like, ah, they're not listening. Oh, I don't know what to do. Oh, I've tried this and they're not doing that. I don't know what to do. I kind of like to take a deep breath and just kind of say, you have this, they trust you. They know your judgment and they know that you have their best interest. So that's a really good.

flow_transcript_slices.question: How do you understand what a nonverbal child needs when they’re crying or upset? Can you walk me through how you respond in those moments?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q11 Attempt 1]
Normally with nonverbal, I've had a few kids that I've worked with, not many, but I remember one little boy would like put his hands up like to be picked up, but he would squeeze his hands kind of like more, but that's when something like would hurt him or he would like point to something. Normally that's like the cues like with their hands or if they fidget a lot. But crying obviously is like the number one, but usually when they're like fidgeting or moving their hands a lot, I would usually that's when I notice they need something. But usually if I know something is wrong, I'll like assess if like they're hurt, if like their stomach is hard, like maybe they're gassy, maybe have to use the restroom. If they want water, sometimes they like look at their water bottle or point at it, give them water.
